items.title: Nepal begins probe into what triggered Bhotekoshi disaster
items.blurb: A seven-member expert panel will trace the August 26 disaster from its source to downstream areas and examine geological, glacial and hydrological hazards, as well as the possible role of climate change.

items.title: Ronaldo, Chitwan’s famed wild elephant, found dead
items.blurb: The bull was a key breeding partner for captive female elephants, with 38 calves attributed to him.

items.title: Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle takes post-disaster reconstruction, climate justice push to global forums
items.blurb: After talks in New Delhi, Wagle is set to raise Nepal’s reconstruction needs and climate vulnerability at upcoming meetings in Doha and Bangkok, with a US visit also being considered.

items.title: Poor rains, poor harvests drive Sudurpaschim Dalits from their villages
items.blurb: Crop failures and landslides are driving families to India and elsewhere, and in the process migration is eroding the traditions, skills and community ties that sustained their villages.

items.title: Jumla waits for its young men who left to earn and never returned
items.blurb: Forty-nine people from Jumla’s Patarasi Rural Municipality remain unaccounted for since the Bhotekoshi floods, including 15 young men from Lamri who had gone to Rasuwa for work.

items.title: Nepal youths begin hunger strike at 4,900 metres over glacial lake risks
items.blurb: Protesters at Manaslu base camp demand monitoring of glacial lakes and measures to reduce climate-related risks.

items.title: 24 days after flood, hunger grips three Rasuwa wards
items.blurb: Food is running out in villages cut off after the Bhotekoshi flood swept away bridges.

items.title: Six bodies recovered from Upper Trishuli-1 tunnel
items.blurb: Rescue teams find the bodies of people missing since the August 26 Bhotekoshi floods as search continues inside the tunnel for possible further victims.

items.title: Two teenage girls rescued while being taken to India on false job promise
items.blurb: Two 16-year-olds from Bardiya were stopped in Banke after officials received a tip-off about their suspected trafficking across the Suiya border point.

items.title: Wagle seeks India’s support for post-flood reconstruction
items.blurb: In his first foreign visit as finance minister, Wagle asks Sitharaman for help in rebuilding infrastructure destroyed by the Bhotekoshi floods and discusses trade, investment and connectivity.

items.title: Bhotekoshi floods disrupt schooling for 14,500 children in three districts
items.blurb: More than 9,400 students have been directly affected, while schools being used as shelters are delaying the return to classes for thousands more.

items.title: Why Nepal’s youth-led government inherited the toughest job in Asia
items.blurb: Wedged between nuclear giants and battered by melting glaciers, Nepal’s untested new leadership faces a test of survival and strategic equilibrium.

items.title: Answer the mountain’s call
items.blurb: Nepal’s government must respond to the disasters with greater accountability and leadership.
